summary: GRAMMER AG’s Americas segment posted an operating EBIT loss of EUR 6.2 million in H1 2026, driven by extra logistics and tariff costs [1]. Group revenue was essentially flat at EUR 961.4 million in H1 2026 (+0.8 % reported, +2.7 % currency‑adjusted) while Americas revenue fell 7.7 % YoY to EUR 153.0 million, making the region a drag on overall resilience [4] [5]. Operating EBIT jumped to EUR 75.1 million in FY 2025 from EUR 41.6 million a year earlier, yet an accumulated loss of EUR –244.1 million remained at 31 Dec 2025 [6] [7]. Equity rose 13.8 % to EUR 317.0 million (equity ratio 18.4 %) by 30 Jun 2026, but current liabilities surged 44.8 % to EUR 878.5 million, signalling a shift toward short‑term funding [9]. Sub‑tier visibility remains limited: despite a Supplier Code of Conduct, LkSG compliance and a whistle‑blowing system, no concrete Tier‑2 mapping, audit results or KPIs are disclosed [10] [11] [12] [13] [14]. ESG targets are set – a 25 % Scope 1&2 CO₂ reduction achieved by 2025, 50 % by 2030, and a 20 % upstream Scope 3 reduction by 2030 – with EcoVadis rating improving to 71 points [15] [18].

report.headline: GRAMMER AG: Profitability up but accumulated loss persists

findings.text: Operating EBIT rose sharply to EUR 75.1 million in FY 2025 from EUR 41.6 million in FY 2024, driven by the “Top 10” program, restructuring and seasonal capacity adjustments.
The company still carried an accumulated loss of EUR –244.1 million as of 31 Dec 2025, only modestly improved from EUR –261.3 million a year earlier.
FY 2025 net income was EUR 17.2 million, reversing a EUR –115.2 million net loss in FY 2024.
Dividend payments are suspended until 2027 under the renewed loan agreement, signalling lender-imposed cash retention.
Equity grew 13.8% to EUR 317.0 million by 30 Jun 2026 (from EUR 278.6 million at end-2025), lifting the equity ratio to 18.4% from 17.3%.
